interface.longDescription: An additive ChatGPT adapter for the original DeepWiki Skill. Version 2.0.13 adds locale-aware Wiki filenames and validation, alongside source-grounded execution lifecycle analysis, evidence excerpts and exact page/diagram anchors, automated cross-file Wiki validation, and expanded regression tests. It preserves the six-phase workflow and keeps the root APM Agent Skill version independent.
interface.defaultPrompt: Use DeepWiki's original six-phase workflow and preserve the workflow-runner contract. Resolve the Wiki locale before TOC design; localize Markdown filenames as well as titles/body/diagram labels. For zh locales require Chinese-script filenames (e.g. 01_项目总览.md); for en use English filenames. Keep page IDs and source identifiers stable. TOC filename is authoritative; update README, TOC, architecture/coverage reports and relative links on rename. Run tools/architecture/validate_toc_filenames.py <toc.yaml>; locale mismatch, duplicate, missing page, or stale link blocks validation. Plugin release version is 2.0.13; the repository-root APM Agent Skill has its own independent version and must not be conflated with the ChatGPT adapter. Before TOC design, page writing, or validation, read references/architecture-completeness.md and references/execution-lifecycle-analysis.md. Do not equate structure, citation count, Mermaid syntax, content completeness, or execution lifecycle coverage. Phase 2 must inspect build manifests, pre-entry registration, entry points, implementation files, tests, and conditional/platform branches; produce _context/architecture_map.json with relevant source inventory, key symbols, directed relationships (compile inputs, includes/imports, link dependencies, runtime entry/call paths, control/data flow, lifecycle/ownership, events/reporting, platform/configuration branches, and test mappings), and page/section/diagram scopes. For significant end-to-end runtime paths, map bootstrap, initialization, dispatch/loop, alternate paths, reporting, and teardown from source; never copy another framework's lifecycle. Phase 3 must create page-local ledgers for critical/supporting claims and relationships with exact line ranges, literal contains excerpts, and exact Markdown anchors or diagram_id + diagram_fragment. Build lifecycle rails, call hierarchies, and event/cleanup diagrams where source supports them; label each edge semantic and include every critical in-scope relationship. Phase 4 must independently re-open key source files and reconstruct behavior, then run tools/architecture/validate_coverage.py and tools/architecture/audit_wiki.py <repo-root> --wiki-dir docs/wiki --output docs/wiki/_reports/cross_file_audit.json. The cross-file gate checks real source line ranges/excerpts, pinned Markdown citations, page and diagram markers, ledger/map relationship identity, and diagram fragments. Its string checks do not prove semantic truth or discover omissions from both ledgers; independent source reread remains mandatory. Keep structure, citations, content coverage, lifecycle coverage, diagram semantics, Mermaid authoring, cross-file audit, and Mermaid renderer statuses separate. Any unreviewed item, coverage gap, failed cross-file check, or critical diagram omission blocks a pass. Run tools/architecture/check_versions.py and both packaged unittest suites. Before Mermaid authoring, read references/mermaid-authoring.md and references/mermaid-engine.md; static lint is not parsing. Renderer passes only after actual Mermaid.js parse + SVG render or Mermaid CLI success; otherwise not_run. Use native page workers only when genuinely supported; otherwise report sequential fallback.
